newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ACCC won't oppose Hoechst Australia unit sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ACCC won't oppose Hoechst Australia unit sale.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Friday it would not intervene in the acquisition of Hoechst AG's Australian plastics business by Kemcor Australia Ltd.
Kemcor is a joint venture between oil majors Mobil Corp and Exxon Corp. The ACCC said it found the acquisition was not likely to substantially lessen competition.
Hoechst announced in January that it had agreed to sell its Australian plastics business to Kemcor for an undisclosed sum.
Under the deal, sealed in a memorandum of understanding, Hoechst's Australian plastics operation at the Altona refinery in Melbourne would be sold to Kemcor, the parties have said.
Kemcor, which makes the feedstock consumed in all of the plastics resin-making at Altona, said the purchase would double its plastics production capacity to 260,000 tonnes per annum.
The move would make Kemcor the biggest producer of polyethylene and polypropylene plastics in Australia.
The ACCC said inquiries it had undertaken indicated that imports were readily available and that the quality of imported high density polyethylene was satisfactory.
